ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the infinitely long wires all carry a constant current I; the straight parts nearly coincide with the coordinate axes, and the curved parts are arcs of the same radius centered at the coordinate origin O. It is known that the straight parts do not form a magnetic field at the origin O, and that the magnetic induction intensity produced at the origin by the arc current in the first quadrant is B. Now a small section of current-carrying wire P, coinciding with the x-axis and of length L, is placed at the origin O (it may be regarded as a current element). The current in wire P has magnitude I and is directed along the positive direction of the x-axis. Then the magnitude and direction of the Ampere force on the current-carrying wire P are
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: 2BIL, with the direction the same as the positive direction of the y-axis

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the coordinate axes take O as the origin, the x-axis points to the right, and the y-axis points upward; the straight parts of the infinitely long wires are close to the coordinate axes, and the curved parts are quarter-circle arcs centered at O and having the same radius. The arrows in the figure mark the directions of the currents in each arc around O, and it can be seen that the contribution of the clockwise arc currents is two more than that of the counterclockwise ones. Then reason: the problem states that the straight parts do not form a magnetic field at O, so only the arc parts need be considered. The magnetic induction intensity produced at O by the first-quadrant arc has magnitude B; since all arcs have the same radius, the same current, and the same central angle, the magnitude of the magnetic field produced at O by each quarter-circle arc is also B. According to the right-hand screw rule, a clockwise current produces a magnetic field at O perpendicular to the paper inward, while a counterclockwise current produces a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper outward; clockwise currents exceed counterclockwise currents by two, so the resultant magnetic field has magnitude 2B and direction perpendicular to the paper inward, namely the -z direction. The small wire P placed at O has current along the positive direction of the x-axis and length L, so the current element direction is +x. By the Ampere force formula F = I L × B, the cross product of +x and -z gives +y, and the magnitude is I·L·2B = 2BIL.
